# Load prerequisite

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(here)
library(ggstatsplot)
library(ggplot2)
library(hrbrthemes)
library(ggh4x)

monthly_pairs <- read_csv(
  here("00_data", "processed", "lst_cooling_pairs_monthly.csv"),
  col_types = cols(
  solar_time = col_character(),
  .default = col_guess()
  )
)

monthly_pairs

```

```{r}
# filter to include only the hottest months (based on monthly air temp)
monthly_pairs <- monthly_pairs |>
  filter(
    (year == 2021 & month == 3) |
    (year == 2022 & month == 2) |
    (year == 2023 & month == 2) |
    (year == 2024 & month == 3)
  ) |>
  mutate(year = factor(year))

```

```{r}
# test for normality --> no evidence against normal destribution
years <- c(2021, 2022, 2023, 2024)
solar_time <- c("13:30","01:30")

for (yr in years) {
  for (st in solar_time) {
    n <- 0
    x <- monthly_pairs |>
      filter(year == yr & solar_time == st) |>
      pull(cooling)

    cat("\nYear:", yr, "| Solar time:", st, "\n")
    print(shapiro.test(x))
    n
    n <- n+1
  }
}

#check min and max cooling for each year
monthly_pairs |>
  group_by(year, solar_time) |>
  summarise(
    min_cooling = round(min(cooling, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    max_cooling = round(max(cooling, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    mean_cooling = round(mean(cooling, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    sd_cooling = round(sd(cooling, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
  )

# get statistics for all reference years
monthly_pairs |>
  filter(year %in% c(2021, 2022, 2023)) |>
  group_by(year, solar_time) |>
  summarise(
    min_cooling = min(cooling, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_cooling = max(cooling, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_cooling = mean(cooling, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_cooling = sd(cooling, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  group_by(solar_time) |>
  summarise(
    avg_min = round(mean(min_cooling), 2),
    avg_max = round(mean(max_cooling), 2),
    avg_mean = round(mean(mean_cooling), 2),
    avg_sd = round(mean(sd_cooling), 2)
  )


```

# Plot Cooling ggbetweenstats

```{r}

solar_time <- c("13:30","01:30")
  
for (st in solar_time) {
  # plot dif for hottest month Tair
  p <- ggbetweenstats(
    data = monthly_pairs |> filter(solar_time == st),
    x = year, 
    y = cooling,
    bf.message = FALSE,
    results.subtitle = FALSE,
    pairwise.alpha = 0.0005,
      point.args = list(
      size = 2,
      alpha = 0.4,
      position = ggplot2::position_jitter(width = 0.14, height = 0)
    )
  ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(
      "2021" = "#A3BDB4",
      "2022" = "#648D80",
      "2023" = "#365F53",
      "2024" = "#FF4500"
    )
  ) + scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = seq(-13,2, by = 2)
    )+
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(2, -14)
  )+
    labs(
      x = "Year",
      y = "Forest cooling (°C)"
    ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14)

  print(p)
  }


```

# Statistics

### Prepare the data for the statistical tests

#### Cooling

```{r}
# First: reshape your data into paired format for 2021 and 2024 comparison
df_wide <- monthly_pairs |>
  # filter(solar_time == "01:30") |>
  select(poly_id, year, cooling,elv_mean, solar_time) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = cooling)

df_wide


```

```{r}
# Quick sanity check
df_wide_test <- df_wide |>
  filter(solar_time == "13:30") |>
  mutate(diff = `2024` - `2021`)

summary(df_wide_test$diff)
hist(df_wide_test$diff)

# !!!! difference distribution seems slightly skewed. Check what to do in this case
```

#### 

### Hypothesis (important)

Because you *expect 2024 \> 2021*, this is a **one-sided paired test**.

**Null hypothesis (H₀):**

H0: μ2024−μ2021=0

(no change in cooling )

**Alternative hypothesis (H₁):**

H1: μ2024−μ2021\>0

(2024 is warmer on average)

#### Compare El Nino year (2024) to all reference years (2021, 2022, 2023)

```{r}

df = df_wide |> filter(solar_time == "13:30")
# df = df_wide |> filter(solar_time == "01:30")

# Run the paired t-test in R
test1 <- t.test(df$`2024`, df$`2021`,
       paired = TRUE,
       alternative = "less")

# Run the paired t-test in R
test2 <- t.test(df$`2024`, df$`2022`,
       paired = TRUE,
       alternative = "less")

# Run the paired t-test in R
test3 <- t.test(df$`2024`, df$`2023`,
       paired = TRUE,
       alternative = "less")
test1
test2
test3
# Bind the p values all together to perform multiple testing
p <- c(test1$p.value, test2$p.value, test3$p.value)
test1$p.value
test2$p.value
test3$p.value

# perform multiple testing with Bonferony Holm
p.adjust(p, method = "holm", n = length(p))
```

#### Compare all reference years (2021, 2022, 2023) among each other

```{r}
# test and plot the difference between the reference years
df_cool_reference_years <- monthly_pairs |>
  filter(solar_time == "13:30") |>
  # filter(solar_time == "01:30") |>
  filter(
    (year == 2021) |
    (year == 2022) |
    (year == 2023)
#     (year == 2024 & month == 4)
  )

# Welch's one-way ANOVA
oneway.test(
  cooling ~ year,
  data =df_cool_reference_years,
  var.equal = FALSE
)



```

# Elevations correlation

###  Linear relationship (facet grid)

```{r}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. Calculate correlation and regression statistics
# --------------------------------------------------

stats <- monthly_pairs |>
  group_by(year, solar_time) |>
  summarise(
    r = cor(
      elv_mean,
      cooling,
      use = "complete.obs"
    ),

    b = coef(
      lm(cooling ~ elv_mean)
    )[2],
    RSE = sigma(
      lm(cooling ~ elv_mean)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. Format labels for each panel
# --------------------------------------------------

stats <- stats |>
  mutate(
    label = paste0(
      "r = ", sprintf("%.2f", r),
      "; b = ", sprintf("%.3f", b),
      "\nRSE = ", sprintf("%.2f", RSE)
    )
  )

# Check the statistics
stats

# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. Create the figure
# -------------------------------------------------

p <- ggplot(
  monthly_pairs,
  aes(
    x = elv_mean,
    y = cooling
  )
) +
  # Points
  geom_point(
    size = 1.5,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +
# One linear regression per panel
geom_smooth(
  method = "lm",
  se = TRUE,
  level = 0.95,
  linewidth = 0.8,
  color = "grey30",
  fill = "grey40",
  alpha = 0.15
) +
# Add r, slope and RSE --> for linear model
geom_text(
  data = stats,
  aes(
    x = Inf,
    y = Inf,
    label = label
  ),
  inherit.aes = FALSE,
  hjust = 1.1,
  vjust = 1.3,
  size = 3.2
) +

# Rows = response variables
# Columns = years
facet_grid(
  solar_time ~ year
) +
  labs(
    x = "Elevation (m)",
    y = "Forest cooling (°C)"
  ) +

 theme_gray()

p
```

### Local min and max LOESS

```{r}

get_loess_turning_points <- function(df) {

  mod <- loess(cooling ~ elv_mean, data = df)

  elev_grid <- seq(
    min(df$elv_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(df$elv_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    length.out = 1000
  )

  pred <- predict(
    mod,
    newdata = data.frame(elv_mean = elev_grid)
  )

  # Remove any NA predictions
  tmp <- data.frame(
    elv_mean = elev_grid,
    cooling_fit = pred
  ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(cooling_fit))

  # Change in sign of the fitted slope
  slope_sign <- sign(diff(tmp$cooling_fit))
  turning <- diff(slope_sign)

  max_idx <- which(turning < 0) + 1
  min_idx <- which(turning > 0) + 1

  bind_rows(
    data.frame(
      type = "local_maximum",
      elv_mean = tmp$elv_mean[max_idx],
      fitted_cooling = tmp$cooling_fit[max_idx]
    ),
    data.frame(
      type = "local_minimum",
      elv_mean = tmp$elv_mean[min_idx],
      fitted_cooling = tmp$cooling_fit[min_idx]
    )
  )
}

# Check local minimum and local maximum for each year
turning_points <- monthly_pairs |>
  group_by(year, solar_time) |>
  group_modify(~ get_loess_turning_points(.x)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(year,solar_time, type)

turning_points

turning_points |>
  arrange(type,elv_mean) |>
  group_by(year, type, solar_time)|>
  summarize(
    mean_fitted_cooling = round(mean(fitted_cooling),2)
  )
```
